slides.label: 1-Forms
slides.notes: Open Act V by changing the classroom question. In earlier chapters an arrow was often the main probe: where does it point, how does it move, how does it rotate? A 1-form asks a different question. Give it a tangent vector and it returns a number. The route for the lecture is intentionally concrete: measuring stacks, work, the differential df, coordinate probes, addition, and then line integrals.

slides.label: A Covector Measures A Tangent Vector
slides.notes: Make the definition operational. A 1-form at p is a linear measurement on the tangent space at p. In the grid picture, the blue parallel slices are not arrows of a vector field; they are level sets of a measuring device. A vector crossing more slices receives a larger value, and reversing the vector reverses the sign. This is the first useful mental model for a covector.

slides.label: Vectors Point, 1-Forms Test
slides.notes: This slide separates the two dual objects. A tangent vector is drawn as a directed displacement. A covector is drawn as a family of equally spaced testing lines. Algebraically this is the difference between a column and a row. The pairing is a scalar, and that scalar survives changes of basis because vector components and covector coefficients compensate.

slides.label: Work Is A 1-Form Field
slides.notes: Use work to make the definition physical. A force or gravitational field becomes a covector field when the question is how much work is done by a small displacement. At each point the 1-form evaluates the velocity or displacement vector. Summing those tiny scalar measurements along a path is the line integral, so line integrals start as local one-form evaluations.

slides.label: The Differential df Is The Prototype
slides.notes: Now connect the measurement picture to functions. The differential df at p eats a tangent vector v and returns the directional change of f in that direction. The contour figure makes this visual: movement tangent to a level curve gives near zero change, while movement across contours gives a larger value. The gradient vector appears only after a metric identifies covectors with vectors.

slides.label: Basis 1-Forms Are Coordinate Probes
slides.notes: Introduce dx and dy as probes rather than mysterious infinitesimals. The form dx asks for the x-component of a tangent vector; dy asks for the y-component. A general 1-form a dx plus b dy combines those probes with weights. This is the practical bridge from diagrams to row-vector algebra.

slides.label: 1-Forms Add By Superposing Measurements
slides.notes: Linearity has a visible interpretation. Scaling a 1-form changes the spacing or sign of its measuring stacks. Adding two 1-forms means measuring with both and adding the scalar answers. The formula is simple, but the slide keeps the geometric meaning in view: covectors form a vector space because measurements can be combined before or after evaluation.

slides.label: Line Integrals Add Local Measurements
slides.notes: Build the line integral as a Riemann sum of local covector readings along a curve. The tangent vector gamma prime is the directed piece of motion, and the 1-form reads that tangent at each point. This prevents a common mistake: the integral is not adding arrows along the curve; it is adding scalar readings produced by the 1-form.

slides.label: Takeaways And Diagnostic Questions
slides.notes: Close with the durable distinctions. A 1-form is a linear functional on tangent vectors, a differential df measures directional change, basis forms extract components, and line integrals sum local measurements along paths. Use the short diagnostics to check whether students are seeing covectors as measurement devices rather than disguised vectors.
